critical_code_review_comments: WebhookController::handleInboundAutomation: the awaiting-reschedule branch does not sanity-check the length or datetime-parseability of the incoming body. Any inbound TEXT (even an emoji reaction like '👍') from a lead with bot_state.reschedule=true will be recorded as their 'preferred slot' and immediately overwrite the BDM's task title. Consider (a) requiring a Carbon-parseable date OR minimum length, (b) capping repeated overwrites, (c) also clearing bot_state on any status change so a stale reschedule flag can't leak into an unrelated future conversation.

WebhookController::handleInboundAutomation deactivates ALL active VisitEngagement rows for the lead on 'resched' without checking that the reply was triggered from a currently-active nudge. If a customer taps an old 'Reschedule' button from a previous engagement (WhatsApp preserves button history), it will still stop the current loop — consider correlating on the source_msg_id or timestamp.

SalesDashboardController::calendarFull unions visits+tasks into a plain list without a stable secondary sort — items sharing the same 'at' timestamp will render in a non-deterministic order between page loads.

Journey Builder client-side (public/assets/js/journey.js) — read-only continuation lanes are enforced only in the SPA (skipped during compile). There is no server-side guard that rejects a mutating save that includes B1/B2/B3/B4/PS lane keys, so a crafted PUT could still overwrite auto-lanes.

SiteVisitService::reschedule calls engagement->start() unconditionally — if the new scheduled_at is < ~1 day in the future, EngagementService::start() will still create a row with total_sends=1 or edge to 0; assert-and-skip on very short horizons would prevent noisy 1-nudge loops.
